_readme: Shipped-size budgets for the web build, enforced by scripts/checkBundleSize.mjs (ASSET_PACKAGING §13). Any "_"-prefixed key is a comment. These are ABSOLUTE budgets with deliberate headroom, not high-water marks: raising one is a decision that needs a written reason here, the same way a file-length-baseline entry does. If a number goes red, the first question is what got bigger and whether it had to.
_measured: Baselined 2026-08-25 against the TARGET=web production build: entry.brotli 470.9 KiB, boot.gate 694.2 KiB, dist.total 22.9 MiB.

entry.brotli.reason: 550 KiB — ~17% over the 470.9 KiB measured 2026-08-25. The bundle is deliberately NOT code-split (user decision, ASSET_PACKAGING §7 item 3: WeChat has no runtime import(), the native shell shortcuts everything locally, so only Web could benefit) — which is exactly why it needs a ceiling instead. It has already grown from the ~1.5 MB raw recorded in §1 to 2.08 MB raw with nobody noticing. Note this is local brotli q11; Cloudflare compresses on the fly at a lower quality and serves ~600 KB for the same file. The local figure is the stable relative metric, not a prediction of the wire size.

boot.gate.reason: 850 KiB — raised from 800 on 2026-08-27, and the headroom is now TIGHTER than before (3.4% over the 822.4 KiB measured that day, vs the old 15% over 694.2). What got bigger: icons_atlas.png went 166 -> 294 KiB because the 2026-08-27 repack stopped palette-quantising it (ASSET_PACKAGING §16). It had to — quantising was silently drifting 97.8% of that page's pixels, alpha by up to 63/255 — and the same repack cut the page's decoded texture from 6.00 MB to 1.54 MB, which is the resource ADR-073 made a budget. So this is a correctness fix with an intrinsic byte cost, not bloat: ~128 KiB of CDN-cached, once-per-client wire bytes bought 4.5 MB of resident VRAM back. The tight new headroom is deliberate and says what the old reason said: THIS tier is now close to its real ceiling, so the next addition is not a raise. The identified next move, if it needs one, is taking icons_atlas OUT of the blocking tier — all three of its consumers already degrade to procedural glyphs (equipmentAtlas/materialAtlas/factionIcon), so nothing breaks; what it needs is a re-await at the icon entrances (equipment bag / card detail / gacha reveal / reward rows) the way §11.2 gave the .tao rigs `ensureBattleAssets`, or an explicit decision to accept a one-frame glyph pop on first open. That is a boot-behaviour change with its own visual verification, deliberately not bundled into the repack.

dist.total.reason: 26000 KiB — ~11% over the 22.9 MiB measured 2026-08-25. Catches art bloat that the two gates above cannot see, because most assets are L1 and neither blocks boot. Matters most for the targets that inherit this figure wholesale: the native shell packages it and the WeChat build has a hard 4 MB main-package limit with the rest on CDN.
